testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: When checking your brakes, a slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from where it attaches to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Check each slack adjuster after setting wheel chocks and disengaging the parking brake. Pull the slack adjusters to make sure they do not move more than one inch from the push rod. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment.

questions.question: Water and compressor oil are normally found in the compressed air in an air brake system. Water and compressor oil:

options.text: Are necessary for the air brake system to work properly.
Should be added when they run low.
Should be removed on a regular basis.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be removed on a regular basis.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system normally contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Open air tank drains every day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What is removed when you drain an air tank?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up in the system.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes:
questions.explanation: To stop normally with air brakes, press down on the brake pedal.

questions.question: A dual air brake system:

options.text: Has one brake system but uses two sets of controls.
Has one brake system for each side of the truck.
Has two brakes for each wheel.
Has two separate brake systems but uses one set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has two separate brake systems but uses one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems that share one set of controls. One system controls the rear brakes. The other system controls the front brakes.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Allow rainwater to enter the tanks.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system normally contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Open air tank drains every day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Brake fading happens when:
questions.explanation: Using the brakes too much causes them to overheat and become less effective. This is called brake fading.

questions.question: A tank endorsement is:

options.text: Required when transporting both liquids and gases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required when transporting both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: A tank endorsement is required to operate a tank vehicle used to transport liquids or gases.

questions.question: On a truck with air brakes, the air compressor:

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. It is controlled by the air compressor governor.

questions.question: A vehicle with air brakes traveling at 55 mph under good conditions needs about ____ to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes four parts: perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle at 55 mph on good roads needs about 450 feet to stop.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a front brake limiting valve, what should you do?

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Keep the control at the halfway mark.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Keep it on "normal" for safe braking.

questions.question: For a double combination vehicle with air brakes, what is the maximum air leakage allowed during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: Air leakage must not exceed 3 psi per minute. If leakage is faster, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs to be repaired.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: To stop normally with air brakes, push the brake pedal down. The harder you press, the more air pressure is released to the brakes.

questions.question: What is the stab braking method for emergency stops?

options.text: Apply brakes fully until wheels lock, release until wheels roll, then repeat.
Apply brakes halfway while keeping wheels rolling.
Apply brakes fully, lock the wheels, and hold until the vehicle stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply brakes fully until wheels lock, release until wheels roll, then repeat.
questions.explanation: Stab braking means applying brakes fully until wheels lock, releasing until wheels roll again, then repeating this pattern.

questions.question: What happens if you press and release the brake pedal too many times?

options.text: Air is released faster than the compressor can replace it.
More air is added to the braking system.
The brake pedal becomes more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air is released faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too many times removes air faster than the compressor can replace it.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is applied to the brakes.
The temperature of the air in the braking system.
The pressure of air from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. Not all vehicles have this gauge.

questions.question: What must truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other air brake vehicles must have ABS if built after March 1, 1998.

questions.question: During inspection, brake drums should have no cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check brake drums before each trip. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half the width of the friction area.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park the vehicle.
To stop the vehicle during normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Apply the parking brake every time you park your vehicle.

questions.question: The emergency brake system uses:

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system.
Only parts of the service brake system.
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems.
Only parts that belong only to the emergency brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems.
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three different brake systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking brake system and the service brake system.

questions.question: If the air pressure warning light comes on, you should:

options.text: Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.
Leave the road safely and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the road safely and stop.
questions.explanation: If the air pressure warning light or buzzer comes on while driving, stop immediately and park safely. This warning means there is a problem in the air brake system that needs repair.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should make sure the spring brakes turn on automatically when:
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, test that the spring brakes turn on automatically when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Block the wheels and release air by pressing and releasing the brake pedal. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve should pop out and the spring brakes should engage.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while you are driving:

options.text: You can only brake if enough air remains in the tanks.
You can apply the brakes 14 times before all air runs out.
Drive normally and check the brakes later when convenient.
Stay at least 100 feet away from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only brake if enough air remains in the tanks.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on while driving a vehicle with air brakes, stop and park safely as soon as possible. There may be a leak. You can only brake as long as enough air stays in the tanks.

questions.question: For a vehicle with air brakes, the air compressor drive belt should be checked before each drive. What condition should the belt be in?
questions.explanation: When checking a vehicle with air brakes that has a belt-driven air compressor, inspect the belt condition and tightness. The belt should be tight and in good condition.
